end.summary:
Navya discussed the story “The Cap-seller and the Monkeys.”
They explained that the monkeys copied the cap-seller’s action.
They retold that he threw down his cap, the monkeys copied him, and he collected the caps.
Navya asked whether the monkeys might keep the caps, then restated the ending correctly.
Teach-back was not completed; Navya asked to stop after a short session.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the story’s cause-and-effect sequence through questions and retelling. Navya connected the monkeys’ copying to a cartoon example and later correctly stated that the caps were thrown down and collected. There was a brief mix-up about whether the monkeys might keep the caps, and Navya corrected the story ending later in the lesson. At home, ask Navya to retell the story in three parts: what the seller did, what the monkeys copied, and what happened at the end.
